title: Air-bridge offline registry design notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for an "air-bridge" pattern: design notes for creating and operating offline registries and curated dependency bundles for air-gapped/private Redwood Inference installs. Focus is on reproducible mirroring, Terraform module interfaces, signed bundle distribution (sneakernet or network-limited), and safe upgrade/rollback semantics.

Scope / assumptions:
- Target audience: infra engineers, solutions eng, and SREs preparing customer on-prem or VPC disconnected installs.
- We assume customers may have no egress, one-way egress (pull proxy), or very limited outbound windows.
- Workflows must cover both network-assisted mirroring (customer allows specific egress) and physical transfer via USB/portable registry (OCI layout).
- We are producing guidance, Terraform module input/outputs, operator notes, and a lightweight verification harness.

High-level patterns:
1) Mirror-and-seed: Operator runs a curated mirror job that pulls images/artifacts into an offline registry inside customer network. When egress is restricted, use an "air-bridge" host in a DMZ to pull and push to an external storage medium.
2) Bundle-and-sign: Produce signed bundles (OCI layout + manifest + checksums + signature) that contain images, Helm charts, manifest.yaml and a dependency lock file. Transfer via secure physical transport.
3) Proxy-seed-window: If customer allows scheduled egress windows, perform batched syncs with strong idempotency and progress checkpoints.

Bundle format spec (proposal):
- layout/: OCI layout directory (compatible with skopeo copy --src-tls-verify=false dir:)
- manifests/: Top-level YAML files: bundles.yml (bundle descriptor), lock.json (artifact list + digest + size), tf-interface.json (optional module metadata)
- signatures/: cosign signatures for bundle metadata and for an index blob
- checksums.txt: SHA256 checksums for all top-level artifacts and their sizes
- README.txt: install ordering and compatibility notes

Minimal bundle manifest (bundles.yml) fields (YAML):
- id: human-friendly bundle id (e.g., rwinf-offline-20240609)
- version: semver-like for bundle lifecycle
- artifacts: list of {name, type: image|chart|tarball, digest, path, required}
- install_order: ordered list of artifact names for deterministic install
- compatible_runtime: ["17.04.1", "17.05.x"] (runtime/kernel/model interface)

Terraform module interface (notes / suggestions):
- Module name: modules/offline_registry
- Inputs (high level):
  - registry_host (string) - internal FQDN to create DNS entry for offline registry
  - storage_class (string) - PV provisioning
  - auth_mode (enum: basic|oidc|none)
  - allowed_cidrs (list of strings) - customer network allowed ranges
  - node_selector (map) - operator placement hints
  - preseed_bundle_url (string, optional) - local path or http to seed bundle TO pipeline
  - enable_garbage_collection (bool)
- Outputs:
  - registry_push_endpoint (string)
  - registry_read_endpoint (string)
  - seed_status_id (string) - id to wire into orchestration
  - tls_secret_ref (string)

Suggested Terraform responsibilities:
- Create k8s namespace and CRDs for offline-registry-operator
- Provision PVs and storage classes used for blob storage (minio/registry filesystem)
- Wire-in TLS secret retrieval (KMS/HSM integration when available)
- Provide an optional null_resource with local-exec to run a verification script after seed

Mirroring tools and commands (practical):
- Use skopeo/crane for scripted mirroring. Example: skopeo sync --all --src docker --dest dir docker://registry.example.com/myimage dir:/tmp/oci-layout 
- For pushing into a registry inside customer net: crane push oci-layout/registry/index.json oci://internal-reg:5000/myrepo --format oci
- For single-file artifact transport create tarball: tar -czf rwinf-bundle-20240609.tar.gz layout/ manifests/ signatures/ checksums.txt

Signing / verification:
- Sign the bundle index and bundles.yml with cosign (or PGP for environments without cosign). Keep root key management in enterprise KMS.
- Verification steps on target: cosign verify-blob --key <pubkey> bundles.yml.sig bundles.yml && sha256sum -c checksums.txt
- Keep a small verification binary (go) that returns structured exit codes for automation.

Upgrade plan (air-gapped specific):
1) Preflight: verify current cluster bundle lock and runtime compatibility.
2) Canary injection (where possible): seed canary namespaces or staging nodes with new images, run synthetic requests against a local probe.
3) Gradual promotion: update image tags in Helm value-overrides, apply to a small slice of nodes, monitor.
4) Roll-forward window: if no regressions in N minutes, expand.
5) Fast rollback: keep previous bundle on disk with index pointer; operator supports an explicit rollback action that re-tags and re-pushes previous digests.

Verification & health checks (post-seed):
- All artifact digests present in registry: check via registry catalog APIs or index.json.
- Signature verify on bundles.yml and on index root.
- Smoke probes for model loading (small token-limited inference) against a test endpoint.
- Disk usage report and GC dry-run to ensure storage headroom.

Operator / SRE runbook (short):
- Pre-seed checklist: confirm customer transport manifest, KYC of physical media, verify signatures before touching cluster.
- During seed: stream logs to secure central bucket (if allowed) or keep local logs and checksum of log file.
- Post-seed: run the verification tool; if verification fails, halt and escalate to solutions eng.
- Upgrade window: set maintenance window, update consoles to read-only vs write ops, capture metrics baseline.

Edge cases and notes:
- Large model shards: recommend chunked upload with clear reassembly manifest. Document model shard ordering and reassembly tool.
- Air-gapped dependency drift: provide a "diff bundle" format containing only changed artifacts + migration notes to shrink transfers.
- Customer with HSM-only signing: provide flow for them to sign bundle index before import and for us to trust their key via trusted roots.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want a canonical "bundle registry" namespace convention for versions? (e.g., bundles/redwood/<bundle-id>)
- How to provide automated delta-generation tooling in a secure way? (prefer server-side delta builder vs local builder)
- Should the Terraform module include an optional operator image registry that can be swapped for air-gapped optimized images (non-Redwood hosted)?

MVP next steps (concrete):
- Build a tiny verification binary (Go) that verifies signatures + checksums + presence of expected digests (owner: Marcus).
- Draft Terraform module skeleton with inputs above and small README (owner: Priya).
- Create bundle example (small sample) using skopeo + cosign for internal testing (owner: Ava).
- Write a short SRE-runbook and checklist for the field team to follow during first customer seed (owner: Diego).

Appendix: quick example commands
- Create OCI layout from remote registry: skopeo sync --all docker://ghcr.io/redwood/example oci:/tmp/rwinf-oci-layout
- Package bundle: tar -C /tmp/rwinf-oci-layout -czf /tmp/rwinf-bundle.tar.gz layout/ manifests/ signatures/ checksums.txt
- Verify on target: tar -xzf rwinf-bundle.tar.gz && cosign verify-blob --key ./pubkey.pem manifests/bundles.yml.sig manifests/bundles.yml && sha256sum -c checksums.txt

Notes to self (todo / small reminders):
- Add sample tfvars and simple CI job to produce delta bundles.
- Check license implications for redistributing certain third-party OCI images in a bundle.
- Coordinate with Security on key escrow and rotation policy for physical media transfers.
